title: Tokenization & runtime parity audit for fallback model variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Maintain and extend the cross-variant compatibility index used by the smart routing layer to ensure safe fallback to model variants. This ticket covers tokenizer parity checks, context-length compatibility, and runtime/tooling feature flags (function calling, streaming, structured output).

Goals:
- Produce an authoritative compatibility index mapping canonical model variants to supported tokenizers, max context, special tooling hooks (function-calling, streaming, stop-sequences), and known behavioral diffs.
- Add automated CI checks that detect mismatches between model metadata (catalog) and the compatibility index on PRs that introduce new model variants or model upgrades.
- Run a one-time sweep across all hosted/dedicated/private catalog entries, flag mismatches, and create follow-ups for remediation.
- Implement a safe rollout path (canary + staged) for any compatibility changes that affect fallback routing policies to avoid client regressions.

Out of scope: changes to upstream model training or tokenizer internals. This is focused on metadata, tests, CI, and routing policy safeguards.
updates: 2025-02-18 - Aisha created the ticket with initial scope. Noted high customer impact due to recent incidents where clients received truncated outputs after fallback to quantized variants.

2025-02-21 - Spike completed: ran tokenizer equivalence checks for 12 popular variants using small prompt corpus. Found 3 variants with differing special-token handling (newline vs <|endoftext|>) and 2 variants with context misreports in catalog metadata. Results uploaded to Confluence.

2025-02-24 - Decision: adopt canonical tokenizer version tag (tk_v1.3) in model metadata and compatibility index. All new model onboarding must include tokenizer test vectors. Miguel to add to model onboarding checklist.

2025-02-28 - PR opened for CI checks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345 . CI script (compat_check.py) validates tokenizer digest, reported max_context, and feature flags against compatibility index. Requesting review from infra-team.

2025-03-03 - Infra review feedback: CI runtime image needs updated Python deps; suggested moving heavy tokenization tests to nightly job to avoid CI slowness. Miguel updated PR to split quick metadata checks into pre-submit and full-suite into nightly pipeline.

2025-03-05 - Canary plan drafted: apply compatibility index changes via routing-config v2.2 and enable on 10% of hosted traffic in us-west1 for 48h. Telemetry: add event routing.fallback.failure_reason and tag variant_pair to detect increases in generation errors. Rollback if error rate increases > 2x baseline.

2025-03-05 - Next steps: finish remediation tickets for the 5 flagged variants, coordinate with Model Onboarding (Rosa Chen) to add tokenizer test vectors, and add a Console dashboard tile for failed fallback breakdown by variant pair.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility index includes tokenizer digest, canonical tokenizer tag, max_context, supported tooling flags for every active variant in the catalog.
Pre-submit CI checks fail PRs that change model metadata without corresponding compatibility index updates.
Nightly full-suite tokenization parity runs against a representative prompt corpus with automated issue creation for mismatches.
Routing-config v2.2 rollout happens on canary traffic with telemetry capturing variant-pair fallback failures and no customer-facing regressions in canary window.
Documentation updated: Confluence page and model onboarding checklist reference the canonical tokenizer test vectors and the compatibility-index maintenance process.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: CI tokenization checks could produce false positives for models with intentional tokenizer differences. Mitigation: add a whitelist of allowed diffs and require model-owner signoff for those variants.
Risk: Nightly full-suite runs may be expensive. Mitigation: use sampled prompt corpus and incremental runs focused on recently changed variants.

Risk: Rollout changes could surface edge-case regressions in Private deployments. Mitigation: coordinate with Private deployment owners for a parallel canary and require upgradeability checks before enabling routing changes.

Risk: Lack of instrumentation to attribute failures to tokenizer vs runtime. Mitigation: add richer failure_reason codes and capture tokenization mismatch traces for failing requests behind a sampling flag.
stakeholders: Infra Team - CI & runtime image support
estimated_impact: Expected to reduce failed fallback incidents caused by tokenizer/context mismatch by ~70-80% and improve routing reliability for multi-variant deployments.
notes: Be conservative with automatic remapping of fallback targets. Any automated change to routing rules must go through canary and provide an automated rollback. Keep PM and SRE on-call in loop during canary window.
